title: Bokor and Weilerstein’s swan
question: How do the two cellists sustain a melodic phrase above the piano’s repeated attacks?
intro: Judith Bokor’s Columbia F 87 side is dated only circa 1925 in its upstream discography; the exact day and catalogue number on Commons conflict with that source. Alisa Weilerstein and Jason Yoder played Le Cygne at the White House on 4 November 2009. The provisional map covers Bokor 0–150 seconds against Weilerstein 4–155 seconds, excluding opening room sound and post-performance sound; a one-semitone feature correction aligns the pitch profiles without changing either audio stream. Bokor’s recording is admitted under European recording-rights expiry, not composition-only tags or an established US first-publication date.

recordings.label: Judith Bokor
recordings.note: Circa 1925; unidentified pianist. Exact session date disputed; historical Columbia D 9758/F 87, European recording-rights expiry only.

recordings.label: Alisa Weilerstein and Jason Yoder
recordings.note: White House, 4 November; cello and one piano. Performance CC BY 3.0; government recording.

passages.label: The sustained melody
passages.note: Follow the cello between the piano’s attacks. Vibrato and slides are listening questions, not machine-measured differences.

passages.label: Early expansion
passages.note: Compare the contour of the first swell, not the absolute playback level of the two transfers.

passages.label: Middle crest
passages.note: Listen through the crest into the quieter phrase beyond it; these are approximate corresponding passages.

passages.label: Later swell
passages.note: Follow the next ascent and release, attending to accompaniment as well as melody.

passages.label: Closing withdrawal
passages.note: Compare the musical release before the sources’ different surface or post-performance sounds. The map stops before those tails.
